findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-20) the CFO guided Q3 NIM expansion of 7-9 bp from an adjusted 3.58% (Q2 reported 3.63% includes a $1.9m nonaccrual interest recovery worth ~5 bp), then 4-6 bp a quarter after; rebuilding Q3 from that guide (NIM ~3.65-3.67% on ~2% higher average earning assets, non-interest income ~$13m, expense at the CFO's '$50m good run rate', provision ~$11-12m, tax <20%, ~109.6m post-split diluted shares) gives NII ~$160-162m, revenue ~$174-175m and EPS ~$0.81-0.83, i.e. on the $0.82-0.83 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (EPS in line, NII slightly short) closed +2.61%. Q1 2026 (a large EPS beat per aggregator headlines) closed +14.58%. The other five prints sit between -0.04% and +2.67%, except Q3 2025 at -6.80%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: consensus already sits where the company's own guide puts it, which is why this is sized near zero. If the market expected a NIM beat, consensus would not have been cut 2.6% in 30 days and the stock would not be down 6.3% over 20 days.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K release gives the inputs (NIM 3.63%, $1.9m recovery, NII $155.6m, expense $50.0m): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430723/000117184326004772/exh_991.htm. It is the same company source, so the two count once.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-14, five sessions before the print and inside the quarter's blackout window, the board approved the company's first-ever buyback: up to 2m shares (~1.8% of ~109.3m post-split shares, ~$79m at $39.28), running to 2027-12-31. CET1 was 11.83% at Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback exists. In July management said it would 'not take anything off the table' on buybacks. No earlier capital-return surprise appears in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement itself is on the wire and the stock has absorbed it: 5-day run-up +1.42%. What may not be priced is the inference that a bank with a 99.5% loan-to-deposit ratio would not open a first buyback days before reporting a quarter with a credit or funding problem. If the market had taken that read, the stock would have recovered more of its 20-day -6.3%.
findings.independence: The split on 2026-07-20 is a second shareholder-friendly action this year: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3371607/servisfirst-bancshares-inc-announces-two-for-one-stock-split. It is a separate document but the same management signal, so it adds little.

findings.finding: SFBS carries a large real-estate-secured nonaccrual relationship (an analyst on the Q2 call put it at 'nearly $100 million'). The CEO said the properties are being listed for sale and are 'properly reserved'. Nonaccrual loans were $169.7m at Q2 (1.18% of loans), against $68.6m a year earlier, with ACL coverage of nonaccrual at 107%. A Q3 disposition could lift NIM through an interest recovery and cut NPAs, or force a charge-off if the sale clears below the carrying value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SFBS's two largest reactions are -6.80% (Q3 2025) and +14.58% (Q1 2026). The sweep reads both as lumpy credit or NIM surprises. In Q2 2026 a similar large nonaccrual payoff brought a $1.9m recovery and the stock closed +2.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither the sale's timing nor its price is public, so the market cannot price the sign. NPAs at 0.96% of assets are already elevated and visible. If a loss were expected, the bar would be cut for provision, and the 2.6% consensus drift is too small to carry a ~$10m+ charge-off.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K confirms the nonaccrual balance and attributes the year-over-year NPA rise to one real-estate-secured relationship: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430723/000117184326004772/exh_991.htm. It shares the call's subject but is a separate document. Sign: none.

findings.finding: Funding is the binding constraint. At Q2, gross loans were $14.48bn against deposits of $14.55bn (99.5% loan-to-deposit). Q2 ending deposits grew only 1.7% annualised, which management attributed to 'the competitive landscape', while loans grew 15.3% annualised. The bank uses no FHLB advances and no brokered deposits. Management said it expects deposit growth to pick up in H2. If Q3 deposits lagged again, either loan growth slowed or the bank funded at the margin with higher-cost money, and the 4-6 bp forward NIM guide is at risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 slow-deposit quarter with a rising NIM still closed +2.61%. On this record funding commentary has not visibly been punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 deposit flows are unknown until the release. The ratio is public, but the preview coverage centres on EPS and the buyback, not on funding. If the market were worried about funding, the stock would trade at a wider discount, and it sits 14% below its high with no option skew to read.
findings.independence: The Q2 call says the bank has no FHLB or brokered funding and that deposit growth was 'more measured': https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2935469. It is a different document with the same company voice. Rule 4 check: no new financing was raised; the issue is the deposit mix, not distress.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-16 the FOMC raised the fed funds target 25 bp to 3.75-4.00%, two weeks before Q3 ended. SFBS's interest-bearing deposit cost of 2.80% is high-beta: the Q2 10-Q shows liability rates fell 59 bp year over year against 14 bp for loan yields. A hike therefore pushes funding cost up quickly, while the CFO's July NIM path assumed fixed-rate loan repricing, not a hike. The main effect falls on Q4 NIM commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior hike-cycle print is in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not quantified, which is why it is sized small. Variable-rate loans reprice upward at the same time, so the net sign is uncertain.
findings.independence: Proxy. The Q2 10-Q rate-volume table shows liability costs moving more than loan yields: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430723/000117184326005359/sfbs20260630_10q.htm. Regions' Q3 NIM still expanded after the hike, which points the other way.

findings.finding: Regions Financial, the largest bank in SFBS's home market of Birmingham, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-16. Adjusted EPS was $0.73 against a $0.66 consensus; NIM was 3.68% against 3.59% a year earlier; net charge-offs fell to 0.29% from 0.42%; business criticized loans fell to 4.71% from 5.01%. The stock rose about 2.3% premarket. Average deposits fell 1.2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for SFBS against peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed after SFBS last spoke, but SFBS's 5-day run-up of +1.42% suggests some read-through has already been taken. Regions is a much larger, lower-beta franchise, so transmission is partial. The falling deposits at Regions also support the funding concern in the finding above.
findings.independence: S&P/Visible Alpha's Q3 2026 bank preview of 2026-10-09 (not fetchable): https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/10/visible-alpha-breakdown-of-us-banks-third-quarter-2026-earnings-expectations. It is a proxy only.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew to agree or disagree with. Against the -6.3% 20-day run-up and the falling consensus, the mild positive lean is contrarian but small. It rests on a first buyback, a home-market peer beat and long days to cover, against funding and credit risks the market can see.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside guidance): the NIM-guide finding moved from +0.2 to +0.1. The Q3 rebuild lands inside the CFO's own 7-9 bp guide, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect.

Rule 7 (positioning before negatives): short interest checked (~4.8% of shares, 13 days to cover). The funding/NIM negative moved from -0.5 to -0.4 because long days to cover on thin turnover give squeeze fuel.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates ($0.82/$0.83), so sizes are not capped further. The pre-split $1.57 AAII figure was rejected as contradicted.
Rule 5 (macro transmission): the Fed-hike finding stays filed and small at -0.2, marked as a proxy. The Regions peer finding stays at +0.3.
Rule 4 (financing): no financing event. The funding finding is about deposit mix, not distress, and is signed after that check.
